chunks: Ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Mukārī entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him: “Has Allah raised your rank to the point that you claim what your father claimed?” He عليه السلام said to him: “What is with you? May Allah extinguish your light and bring poverty into your house! Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to ʿImrān: ‘Indeed I am granting you a male,’ then He granted him Maryam, and granted to Maryam ʿĪsā. So ʿĪsā is from Maryam, and Maryam is from ʿĪsā, and ʿĪsā and Maryam are one thing; and I am from my father, and my father is from me, and I and my father are one thing.”
Then Ibn Abī Saʿīd said to him: “So I ask you about a question.” He عليه السلام said: “I do not think that you will accept from me, and you are not of my flock, but bring it.”
He said: “A man said at the time of his death: ‘Every slave of mine that is old is free for the sake of Allah, Exalted.’” So he عليه السلام said: “Yes. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:”
“Until it returned like the old date-stalk.”
“So whatever of his slaves has reached six months for him, then it is old and free.”
He said: So he left and fell into poverty until he died, and he did not have a place to spend even one night. May Allah curse him.

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā, the addressed Imam in this report
key_terms.الْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ: The old date-stalk, a Qur’anic phrase used to define ‘old’
key_terms.عِمْرَانَ: ʿImrān, mentioned in the revealed message cited by the Imam
key_terms.عِيسَى: ʿĪsā, invoked to illustrate genealogical and essential connection
key_terms.قَدِيمٌ: Old; here interpreted legally as having reached six months
key_terms.مَرْيَمَ: Maryam, given as the mother of ʿĪsā in the Imam’s analogy
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٍ: An owned slave or bondsman in the legal question

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام explain his relationship to his father and define an “old” slave in a ruling on emancipation?
ai.summary: This report recounts a confrontation with Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام in which he affirms the profound unity between himself and his father, using the example of Maryam and ʿĪsā. It also includes a legal ruling on emancipating slaves described as “old,” deriving the meaning from a Qur’anic expression. The narration closes by reporting the destitution of the questioner as a consequence of his stance.
